title: Effect of Reflective Plastic Mulches on the Microclimate, Photosynthetic Activity and Yield of Pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) in a Multispan Greenhouse
content: Soil mulching materials play an important role in regulating the greenhouse crop microclimate, as they influence light distribution, plant physiological activity, and crop yield. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effects of two plastic mulches (black polypropylene and white polyethylene mulch) on the microclimate, photosynthetic activity, crop development, yield, and fruit quality of sweet pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) grown under greenhouse conditions. The trial was developed during a spring–summer growing cycle in a multispan greenhouse divided into two compartments(sectors) separated by a vertical polyethylene sheet. In the eastern sector of the greenhouse (control treatment), a black polypropylene agrotextile mulch with a thickness of 0.225 μm was installed, while in the western sector, a white polyethylene plastic mulch (black on the inner side) with a thickness of 30 μm was used. The use of white polyethylene mulch resulted in slightly higher mean and maximum PAR inside the greenhouse by up to 3.7 % compared with black polypropylene mulch, leading to slightly higher leaf-level PAR and net photosynthetic rate. Although no significant differences were observed in plant morphology or fruit quality parameters, marketable yield increased by 66% and total yield by 40 % under white polyethylene mulch. Slight increases in internal air temperature were recorded without exceeding critical thresholds, while relative humidity remained largely unaffected. The use of reflective mulches represents a low-cost and sustainable strategy to improve pepper yield and radiation-use efficiency in passively ventilated greenhouse systems under Mediterranean climatic conditions.
